subject: general
question: Pranjal takes twice as much time as Vikram or thrice as much time as Ashwin to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 6 days. Vikram can do the work alone in:
solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pranjal = Twice as much as Vikram

Time taken by Pranjal = Thrice as much as Ashwin

Time taken to finish work together = 6 days

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let Pranjal take x days to complete the work.

⇒ So, Vikram takes (x)/(2) and Ashwin takes (x)/(3) days to complete the work.

⇒ According to the question, all working together

⇒ Then, ((1)/(x)+(2)/(x)+(3)/(x) )=(1)/(6)

⇒ (6)/(x)=(1)/(6)

⇒ x = 36 days

⇒ Time taken by Vikram to complete the work = (x)/(2)=(36)/(2)=18 days

**Hence, Vikram can complete the work alone in 18 days.**

**Short trick:**

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total unit/No. of days

Time is inversely proportional to efficiency

**Calculation:**

As , we know that time is inversely proportional to efficiency 

So, let the efficiency of pranjal be x 

Then efficiency of vikram = 2x

Efficiency of Ashwin = 3x

Total efficiencies = x + 2x + 3x = 6x 

Total days taken to work together = 6 

Total unit = 6x × 6 = 36x

Now, vikram can do the work in = 36x/2x = 18

**Hence, vikram can do the work in 18 days .**
